name: Gera
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Schuh, Russell G. 1978. Bole-Tangale Languages of the Bauchi Area (Northern Nigeria). Marburg: Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A13.
earlier_scan.note: Schuh 1978 group study covers Gera; not online, no stress statement read.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. (version May 2011). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 149 'Gera', p. 29.
sources.note: Catalogue entry only: names Gere/Fyandigere/Gerawa, Bauchi and Darazo LGAs, 13,300 (1971), 'Refs. Schuh (1978)'. Nothing linguistic.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gera language' (raw wikitext), citing Ethnologue 25 and Blench 2019 Atlas 4th ed.
sources.note: Classification, autonym Fyandigere, 2018 survey note (4 villages transmitting). No phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Gere-Hausa-English wordlist (June 2006). 8 pp., ms. (rogerblench.info, 'Gere three lang ').
sources.note: Bare wordlist (Gere = Gera); a Notes column carries sporadic tone marks (e.g. bawi 'mouth' [báwî], bigini 'where?' [bìgínî]). No phonology prose, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2005. The totality extension and focus in West Chadic. Paper, International Berlin Focus Conference, 6-8 October 2005. 26 pp.
sources.note: Mentions Gera twice (Schuh 1978 found no totality extension in Kirfi, Galambu, Gera; ICP example 'Gera nì fiɗə̀m jì-m-ni I went out'). Tone marked in examples; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 2005. Yobe State, Nigeria as a linguistic area. Proceedings of BLS 31. 33 pp. (UCLA aflang preprint).
sources.note: Gera named once as a Bauchi-State relative of the Yobe languages. Nothing on Gera phonology or stress.
Lists Schuh 1978 (subclassification comment) and Zoch 2011/2014 as the only descriptive references; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1978. Bole-Tangale languages of the Bauchi Area (Northern Nigeria). Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A13. Berlin: Reimer. XI+159 pp. Gera chapter pp. 91-113, 'Remarks on Phonology' pp. 92-94.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only first-hand sketch of Gera phonology; TOC shows vowel phonetics and tone rules sections (pp. 93-94) where any remark on stress/prominence would sit. Named by the earlier scan and by Blench's Atlas as the sole reference for Gera.

sources.citation: Zoch, Ulrike. 2017. Pluractionals in Bole-Tangale languages (West-Chadic). STUF - Language Typology and Universals 70(1).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Only other peer-reviewed work with Gera data; morphological, so a stress statement is unlikely, but its introduction may summarize the prosodic type.

sources.citation: Zoch, Ulrike. 2014. Verbalmorphologie der Bole-Tangale-Sprachen (Nordostnigeria). Schriften zur Afrikanistik 22. Frankfurt: Peter Lang. 317 pp. (= Diss. Frankfurt 2011). Ch. 2.2 'Ton' pp. 51-55, 2.3 'Silbenstrukturen' p. 55.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Modern comparative description covering Gera among 13 Bole-Tangale languages, with a tone-systems section that may state whether the languages have any stress/accent beyond tone; German.

sources.citation: Zoch, Ulrike. 2011. Vergleichende Aspekte der Morphologie der Bole-Tangale-Sprachen mit besonderer Berücksichtigung des Verbalsystems. PhD diss., Johann Wolfgang Goethe-Universität Frankfurt.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: DNB record for the 2014 book carries 'Zugl.: Frankfurt (Main), Univ., Diss., 2011', i.e. the dissertation is the 2014 book. Frankfurt repository is behind an Anubis JS wall; not opened.
